newsitem.title: FINLAND: RAISIO SEES BENECOL IN U.S. SOON.
newsitem.headline: RAISIO SEES BENECOL IN U.S. SOON.

text.p: Finnish food, animal feed and chemicals group Raisio said on Thursday it expects its cholesterol-reducing agent Benecol to reach the U.S. market in the next few years.

"We will certainly see it on the U.S. market during the next few years," Raisio CEO Matti Salminen told a news conference, but stressed the product may not be sold in the U.S. in margarine form, as it is currently sold in Finland.
Benecol will be the trading name of the fat-soluble stanol ester which Raisio has patented in many countries.
Raisio said turnover on its margarine would reach about 250 million markka in 1996 and 1997, with the largest part in 1997.

Raisio earlier said it was building another factory to produce the stanol ester and would have capacity to esterify 2,000 tonnes yearly -- which Salminen said corresponds to about 20 million tonnes of margarine.
Asked if the company had been in talks with margarine major Unilever on cooperation with the new product, he said: "We have had no talks."
Raisio said its strategy with Benecol was to keep production of the active ingredient in-house and develop partnerships with other companies overseas for the manufacture of the end-product.
"It is clear we will need partners elsewhere in the world to whom we will sell the active agent," Salminen said.
